editorial.headline: The Wholesale Trade Behind Indonesia’s Non-Dairy Drinks
editorial.standfirst: Nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, this wholesale activity is nevertheless blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the island-wide moratorium.
editorial.body:
Wholesale trade in non-dairy beverages is a precisely defined commercial lane. Its scope is the wholesale trade of non-alcoholic drinks other than milk, expressly including fruit nectars, juices, soft drinks, mineral water and packaged water. The category is broad enough to encompass familiar everyday beverages, yet its centre of gravity remains clear: wholesale trade in the listed non-alcoholic products. For an enterprise, the relevance lies in the nature of the products handled and in the wholesale character of the activity.

The activity is open at every scale named in the record—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar—rather than being confined to a single enterprise size. In registration terms, it is available to enterprises at each of those listed scales, from micro through large business. The scale picture is therefore broad, but not vague: the activity remains anchored to the specified beverages and to wholesale trade. The range tells a prospective registrant where it may sit by business size; the scope tells them what activity is being registered.

Nationally, the PMA position is open and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In plain terms, foreign ownership may reach the full stated ceiling under the national setting recorded for this activity. The distinction between an open status and its stated 100% ceiling is useful: the percentage supplies the precise national extent of foreign ownership rather than leaving it implicit. This national picture matters, but it does not settle the question for a business seeking PMA registration in Bali.

In Bali, the conclusion changes sharply. The activity is blocked because, at the Besar scale, OSS risk is Low/Medium-Low across every scope and the Bali moratorium blocks PMA registration on that basis. The moratorium is island-wide and permanent, and the recorded reason identifies it as the Bali moratorium of May 13, 2026. Accordingly, a foreign investor cannot register this activity for PMA in Bali today. This is not a Bali-specific foreign-ownership cap alongside the national 100% ceiling; it is a registration block. National openness does not override Bali’s registration block. For a Bali PMA plan, that local block is the decisive fact.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not override Bali’s registration block.
